requirements.text: Build Verisearch.slnx on .NET 10 with nullable analysis and warnings-as-errors enabled.

Create the sealed positional records `RankedEntry(string Id, int Priority)` and `RankingResult(IReadOnlyList<string> Ids, int Accepted, int Rejected)`. Inside RankingContract, implement `RankedEntry? Parse(string line, char separator)` and `RankingResult Rank(string input, char separator, string failureMode, string outputOrder)`. Rank must call Parse for each retained segment and return the RankingResult that the top-level program writes; dummy members plus a separate inline implementation do not satisfy this public structure contract.

The evaluator supplies at most 10,000 LF-delimited segments that are nonempty before CR handling; larger inputs are outside this contract. LF is the only delimiter and a final unterminated segment is processed. Discard only segments whose length is already zero, then remove one trailing CR from each retained segment; therefore a segment containing only CR becomes an empty rejected record and counts toward the bound, while any other CR is data. A valid record is exactly <identifier><separator><priority>, with no quoting, escaping, or surrounding whitespace. An identifier is 1-16 ASCII characters: an uppercase A-Z first, then only uppercase A-Z, digits, or underscore. Priority is one or more ASCII digits, leading zeroes and zero are allowed, plus/minus signs, whitespace, non-ASCII digits, and values above Int32.MaxValue are rejected. Each valid record remains an independent entry, including duplicate identifiers; malformed records never remove valid entries.

The supplied constants are this candidate's fixed compile-time assignment; no alternate ordering or runtime selector is required. Sort using exactly this assigned algorithm: ordinal identifier ascending. The phrase is exhaustive: `priority descending then ordinal identifier ascending` uses descending integer priority as the primary key and StringComparer.Ordinal identifier as its tie-breaker; `ordinal identifier ascending` uses only StringComparer.Ordinal identifier and priority never participates. Write UTF-8 stdout as exactly six lines: `domain=trail-checkpoint`, `rejection-cap=1`, `order=ordinal identifier ascending`, `ids=` followed by the ordered identifiers joined by commas with no spaces or escaping (or exactly `ids=` when none are accepted), `accepted=` followed by the valid-record count, and `rejected=` followed by the smaller of the malformed-record count and numeric cap 1. Terminate every line, including the sixth, with one LF (U+000A); emit no CR or other text. The 10,000-segment bound prevents count overflow.

rubric.criterion: The assigned behavioral contract is satisfied by a clean build and varied runs.

expect.regex:
\Adomain=trail-checkpoint
rejection-cap=1
(?=order=ordinal identifier ascending
)(?:order=priority descending then ordinal identifier ascending
ids=B,A|order=ordinal identifier ascending
ids=A,B)
accepted=2
rejected=1\Z
